findings.finding: Q3 fees net to about the $3.20bn priced, line against line. FX volumes rose into Q3 rather than moderating: CLS average daily traded volume was $2.658trn in July and $2.730trn in August 2026 against a Q2 average of $2.629trn (+14.7% and +15.4% YoY), and BNY's CFO said volumes 'kicked back into September', while the street has State Street's FX at $443m, -10% QoQ. Against that, the custody peers that printed on 13 Oct grew less than State Street's servicing consensus of +3.5% QoQ ($1.52bn vs $1,468m): JPM Securities Services fell 2% QoQ to $1,626m with period-end AUC -1.7% to $44.1trn, and Citi Securities Services fees rose 2% QoQ with AUC/A flat at $35trn.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed record FX ($494m, +14% QoQ) inside an EPS beat ($3.65 vs ~$3.34) and a raised guide, and the stock fell 0.5% (baseline, 2026-07-16). This name has not paid for fee beats in 2025-26.
findings.why_not_priced: Anchoring on the company's guide: the FX line sits on the CFO's 'some moderation in the markets business' (14 Sept) and the July outlook's 'moderating a bit from the record'. If the CLS volumes were in the number, the FX estimate would sit near flat QoQ, not -10%. The counterweights are sized in: State Street's own CFO had seen July and August when he said moderation, and realised FX volatility fell in Q3 for EUR (4.2% vs 5.3% annualised), GBP (5.2 vs 6.6) and AUD (6.2 vs 9.2), my computation from Yahoo daily closes. So this is a proxy and stays small. The servicing side cuts the other way and is also only partly comparable: on a YoY basis the peers (JPM +14%, Citi fees +13%) match or beat State Street's servicing consensus (+12%), and JPM's Q2 had jumped 10.5% QoQ, so the QoQ dip is partly a high base. Net of both lines the finding is +0.10.

key_questions.answer: Same as priced: no buyback cut. The September bond rout (30 Jun to 30 Sep: 2y +74bp, 5y +90bp, 10y +85bp) costs CET1 only about 10-25bp through AOCI, because State Street's AFS book ($72.3bn; portfolio duration 2.0 years including hedges) has barely moved AOCI in 2026: OCI on securities was -$59m after tax in H1 for a +67bp 2y move and +$72m in Q2 for +35bp. With ~$1.08bn of quarterly earnings, CET1 should land ~10.6-10.9% and repurchases of ~$400m should continue. Consensus already holds this (standardized Tier 1 13.4%, Tier 1 leverage 5.3%).

premortem.other_way_reason: With p_up at 49 the other way is a hard rally. State Street would show Q3 average deposits at or above ~$270bn and NII above $870m, guide Q4 and 2027 NII up on the Fed and ECB hikes, and raise the fee guide to ~14% with operating leverage above 500bp. As the first custody print after BNY's 14 Sept deposit warning, it would unwind part of the group's 11% de-rating (the April 2025 print after a -11.7% run-up rose 2.05%).

premortem.evidence_already_had: H.8 large-bank deposits at a high on 30 Sept; JPM deposits +2% QoQ and Citi Services deposits +16% YoY on 13 Oct; the 10-Q's +$343m per +100bp short-end NII sensitivity; the S&P 500 ~2% above its 30 Sept level.

investment_decision.reason: All five frozen questions came back within about 1% of what the price holds. The street's $3.20bn fees, $857.9m NII and roughly flat expenses sit on the CFO's 14 Sept 'stable quarter-over-quarter' steer (Q1, Q2, Q3). The street's Q3 fee number already implies the ~14% full-year raise (Q5), and the September bond rout costs CET1 only tens of basis points (Q4). The small tilts offset: industry FX volumes and steady large-bank deposits lean up, peers' custody fees growing less than STT's servicing line leans down, the expense tail and a sector that sold Citi's beat on 13 Oct lean down, so impact_sum of -0.30 on a 4.4% scale agrees with not trading.
investment_decision.what_would_change_it: Q3 average deposits and the Q4 NII guide. Deposits at or above ~$275bn with NII guided up on the hikes would make this a long into the custody de-rating. A full-year expense guide at or above ~9% with cost commentary on 2027 would make it a short.
